entry.title: Portable Flashing Package: Rondo 1.0.2
entry.content:
Rondo 1.0.2 is about the server: it now updates itself with one click from its admin page. **Nothing changes on the Y1 itself**; it still offers this version as an update so the Y1 and the server stay on the same number.
## What's new
- **Update the server with one click.** When a newer Rondo is out, the server's admin page offers **Update**: the server downloads the new version and restarts on it in a minute or two, keeping your settings, YouTube account and connected Y1. A small companion container, `rondo-updater`, does the work; it only ever touches the Rondo server's own container, and if the new version doesn't start, the old one comes back by itself. - **Ready-made server images.** Installing the server now downloads it instead of building it on your machine, for regular PCs and 64-bit ARM (Raspberry Pi 4 and 5, many NAS boxes). The first start is much quicker on small machines.
The full list is in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/jarvissax/rondo/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).
## Moving your server over
A server set up before 1.0.2 built itself and has no updater yet. Update it by hand once, and **Update** on the admin page does it from then on:
```bash cd rondo git pull docker compose -f infra/compose.home.yaml pull # or compose.vps.yaml docker compose -f infra/compose.home.yaml up -d ```
Your admin password, YouTube account and connected Y1 stay. Details: [Keeping it running](https://github.com/jarvissax/rondo/blob/main/docs/server.md#keeping-it-running).
## The Y1
If your Y1 runs Rondo 1.0.1, **Settings › Software update**, **Install** in the dashboard or [the update page](https://jarvissax.github.io/rondo/) bring it to 1.0.2 in a minute; nothing else changes. New to Rondo: choose **Rondo** in [Innioasis Updater CE](https://innioasis.app) (Y1, then Type A), or install `rom.zip` below with the Updater's **Settings › Install from a file…**. Only for the **Y1 Type A**.
## Files
- `rom.zip`: the firmware, for Innioasis Updater CE (Y1 Type A), built from `rondo-1.0.2.apk` by the release workflow. - `rondo-1.0.2.apk`: the update, for a Y1 that already runs the Rondo firmware. - `updater.png`: the picture Innioasis Updater CE shows for this release. - The server images: `ghcr.io/jarvissax/rondo-server:1.0.2` and `ghcr.io/jarvissax/rondo-updater:1.0.2` (also `latest`).

entry.title: Portable Flashing Package: Rondo 1.0.1
entry.content:
A small update to Rondo for the **Innioasis Y1, Type A**. If your Y1 already runs Rondo, it installs over the one you have in about a minute, and everything stays: settings, Wi-Fi, server connection, playlists and music.
## What's new
- **Click sound stays off.** Turning off **Settings › Click sound** (or the switch in the dashboard) now lasts through a restart. Before, the Y1's own sound profile turned the click back on every time it started. - **Every release now comes with its firmware.** The `rom.zip` that Innioasis Updater CE installs is built automatically for each release, so a new install always gets the newest Rondo. - **Rondo knows which updates it can install.** The firmware now carries a version of its own. If a future release changes the firmware itself, not only Rondo, Settings › Software update, the dashboard and the update page say so and point you to Innioasis Updater CE, instead of offering an install that couldn't work. - **One place for news of a release.** The Y1 (through your server), the dashboard and the update page all learn about a new Rondo from the update page, once its firmware is ready, so they always agree with each other and with Innioasis Updater CE. - **New README and guides**, with screenshots.
The full list is in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/jarvissax/rondo/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).
## Updating from 1.0.0
Pick whichever is handiest; none of them reinstalls the firmware:
- **On the Y1:** Settings › Software update, then **Install now** (needs your Rondo server). - **In the dashboard:** Settings › Dashboard on the Y1, open it on your phone, press **Install**. - **Over USB:** open [the update page](https://jarvissax.github.io/rondo/) in Chrome or Edge and plug the Y1 in.
If you run a Rondo server, update it too ([how](https://github.com/jarvissax/rondo/blob/main/docs/server.md#keeping-it-running)); it's 1.0.1 as well.
## Installing for the first time
Choose **Rondo** in [Innioasis Updater CE](https://innioasis.app) (Y1, then Type A), or download `rom.zip` below and use the Updater's **Settings › Install from a file…**. Installing replaces everything on the Y1 itself; **the microSD card isn't touched**. The [install guide](https://github.com/jarvissax/rondo/blob/main/docs/install.md) has the details.
Only for the **Y1 Type A** (players that shipped with software 2.0.0 or later), not the Type B or the Y2.
## Files
- `rom.zip`: the firmware, for Innioasis Updater CE (Y1 Type A). Built from `rondo-1.0.1.apk` by this repository's release workflow, a few minutes after publishing. - `rondo-1.0.1.apk`: the update, for a Y1 that already runs the Rondo firmware. - `updater.png`: the picture Innioasis Updater CE shows for this release.

entry.title: Portable Flashing Package: Rondo 1.0.0
entry.content:
Rondo is now a firmware for the Innioasis Y1: the Y1 starts straight into Rondo's click-wheel menus, with nothing else on it.
**For the Y1, Type A only** (players that shipped with software 2.0.0 or later). Not for the Type B or the Y2.
## Install
Choose **Rondo** in [Innioasis Updater CE](https://innioasis.app) (Y1, Type A). Or download `rom.zip` below and use the Updater's **Settings › Install from a file…**.
Installing replaces everything on the Y1 itself: the original player, Rockbox, settings. **The microSD card isn't touched**, so your music stays. When the Updater is done, press the Y1's Power button; the first start takes a couple of minutes. The [install guide](https://github.com/jarvissax/rondo/blob/main/docs/install.md) has the details and the first steps after it.
For YouTube Music and YouTube, [set up a Rondo server](https://github.com/jarvissax/rondo/blob/main/docs/server.md) with Docker, at home or on a VPS.
## Updates
Later versions install over this one in a minute, without flashing again, keeping your settings, Wi-Fi, playlists and music: **Settings › Software update** on the Y1, **Install** in the dashboard, or [the update page](https://jarvissax.github.io/rondo/) over USB.
## What's in it
- iPod-style menus for the click wheel, with optional vibration and a click on every step - Your music and videos from the microSD card, with covers, lyrics, search and playlists - The card as a USB drive when the Y1 is plugged into a computer - YouTube Music and YouTube, streamed live through your own server, including Shorts, with or without a YouTube account - FM radio with station names, scanning and saved stations - Bluetooth headphones and speakers, and Wi-Fi, set up from the wheel - A dashboard in your phone's browser for music, playlists, settings, the theme, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, the radio and updates - Shut down and restart from Settings, or by holding the Power button
## Good to know
- Only the Y1 Type A is supported; the Type B and Y2 haven't been tested. - Rockbox, the original player and Android's own Settings aren't part of Rondo. Innioasis Updater CE puts any of them back. - YouTube Music and YouTube need your own Rondo server; the card, the radio and Bluetooth don't.
## Files
| File | What it is | SHA-256 | | --- | --- | --- | | `rom.zip` | The firmware, for Innioasis Updater CE (Y1 Type A) | `97855240680f2f71f0e33147bd6f7567f4bf17e2efb082d495dc55b2877a0b6c` | | `rondo-1.0.0.apk` | Rondo by itself: updates a Y1 that runs the Rondo firmware | `911edd65b8f375e452c05e2004c1c817215a65f9a56d023c5acfb9a7d0857edd` | | `updater.png` | The picture Innioasis Updater CE shows for this release | `40b9f5679e2f84b4dd7c6fda968abf702df3ccb6b743fcb88e142eeb8b52047e` |
The firmware is built with [`firmware/build.sh`](https://github.com/jarvissax/rondo/blob/main/firmware/build.sh) from the y1-community's [Android 4.2 base ROM](https://github.com/y1-community/y1-ata-rom) (0.1, Type A). Its scatter file, preloader and flashing files are the base ROM's, unchanged.
